about: Draft TC-01 to TC-20, written 2026-11-24, TC-21 to TC-27, written 2026-11-25 for the provisional decisions, TC-28 to TC-34, written 2026-11-25 for Directive as a decision-making coach, TC-35 to TC-39 for the framework handoff, TC-40 for emotional understanding, TC-41 for simple English and remembering what was said, TC-42 and TC-43 for the same scenario in the other two styles, TC-44 to TC-46 for one emotional scenario in each style, and TC-47 to TC-59 for the harder kinds of conversation in muhammad's brief of 2026-11-25 (ambiguous, conflicting, rejected readings, no advice wanted, memory, a change of mind, and a triplet), from the client's documents and real tests; awaiting muhammad's approval. `script` is sent in order (a button's exact label taps it), then `persona` plays the rest. `expect` keys are read by evals/regression/checks.py. A scenario with status `gap` asks for something paused or removed by a Decision in force: it is reported, never run.

scenarios.title: Directive: workplace overload walks ABCDE to the close
sources: muhammad's Test 1 (2026-11-24)
Framework Sequences - Example Conversations
Pacing Rules
Lolly's email, 2026-11-20 (the close is Continue chatting or Visit library; introduce ABCDE)
script: I've been feeling overwhelmed at work lately. I have so many things to do, and I feel like I'm constantly falling behind.
It's mostly because my manager keeps adding new tasks, but I don't feel comfortable saying no.
I feel like if I push back, they'll think I'm not capable of doing my job.
I haven't really said no directly. Sometimes I mention that I'm busy, but then I end up doing the work anyway because I don't want to disappoint anyone.
scenarios.persona: Your manager keeps adding tasks and you never say no because you fear looking incapable and disappointing people. You call your manager 'my manager' or 'they' and never say he or she. Yesterday they handed you another urgent project on top of two deadlines; you agreed, worked late, skipped dinner and still missed one deadline. Last month you told them you couldn't finish a report by Friday and they moved the deadline without fuss. If offered a set of steps, try it and answer each step honestly. When it is finished, say you're done for now.
scenarios.criteria: The offer names the framework and ties it to what they want help with; stays with what they said before offering; never invents details (the manager's gender, events they did not describe); one question a turn; each stage asks something new; Directive is short and leads.

scenarios.title: An upcoming holiday, a past one and two people kept apart
sources: Lolly's Thanksgiving test, email 2026-11-23 (keep past, present and anticipated events apart; no assumptions stated as facts; never move a detail to the wrong person)
script: thanksgiving is this thursday and i'm going to be alone for it. it'll be the first one without my family
last year my parents and i fought through the whole dinner, so this year i'm not going. my friend was going to come over but now my friend is visiting family out of state
scenarios.persona: Thanksgiving has not happened yet; it is this Thursday. Last year you fought with your parents at dinner. Your friend is away visiting their own family. You call them 'my parents', 'my friend' or 'they' and never say he or she. You have a home and people who care about you; you're sad and scared about the day. If Mani treats Thursday as already past, mixes up your parents and your friend, or says something you never said, correct it plainly.
scenarios.criteria: Thursday stays ahead and last year stays past throughout; the fight stays with the parents and the trip with the friend; no circumstance they did not give (nowhere to go, no one at all); the original concern, the coming Thursday, stays the subject.

scenarios.persona: The workload is real: three reports due Friday and a client presentation on Thursday. You call your manager 'my manager' or 'they' and never say he or she. scenarios.title: Directive: a repeated wrong implementation is diagnosed before any personnel step
sources: muhammad's Directive brief and tester's business-owner chat, 2026-11-25
script: I am the business owner and my technical resource is not working properly. I tell him what I want to do but he implements something completely different.
I asked him to rectify a feature and they returned back with the same mistake again.
I told him it's still wrong and they recognised it was wrong and told me they will rectify it but it is the fifth time this exact same thing has happened and I'm tired of doing that now.
That's what I'm confused about.
scenarios.persona: You own a small business. Your developer keeps delivering the wrong feature. If asked, the truth is: you explain changes in quick voice notes, he says he understands, and he builds his own idea of it; there is no written spec and nobody tests before it reaches you. You want this to stop costing you time. Answer what Mani asks plainly; once Mani has understood, you want a concrete plan.
scenarios.criteria: Asks where it breaks down (understanding the request, building it, or testing) before recommending anything; recommends no personnel step before the cause is known; once the cause is clear, gives two or three specific options with reasons and helps pick a first step; never states 'it's him' or any cause as fact.

scenarios.title: Directive: an explicit request for a script is answered at once

script: my landlord hasn't repaired the heating in three weeks and i've asked twice. can you write me the exact text to send him?
scenarios.persona: You rent a flat; the heating has been broken three weeks. You want a firm but polite message you can send today. React to what Mani writes, maybe ask for it a bit firmer.
scenarios.criteria: Writes the message in the first reply, built from their details, offered as theirs to change; no questions instead of the script; no assumption about the landlord they did not state.

scenarios.title: Directive: help choosing between two options weighs them against what matters
sources: muhammad's Directive brief and tester's business-owner chat, 2026-11-25
script: i have a job offer with 20% more pay but a 90 minute commute each way. my current job is 15 minutes away. can you help me decide?
scenarios.persona: You have two young kids and money is tight but not desperate. You lean slightly toward the new job but you're unsure. If asked what matters, say time with your kids and getting out of debt. You want help thinking it through, not a verdict.
scenarios.criteria: Helps at once: sets out what each option gives and costs, asks what matters most if needed, weighs the options against it, treats their slight lean as a preference not a decision, leaves the choice to them, and reaches a next step.

scenarios.title: Directive: a problem explained in full gets options without re-asking
sources: muhammad's Directive brief and tester's business-owner chat, 2026-11-25
script: My manager gives me tasks at 5pm that are due the next morning, about three times a week. I've already told her twice that I need more notice and she agreed but nothing changed. I'm not quitting, I like the job. I want it to stop. What should I do?
scenarios.persona: You've explained everything already. If Mani asks for things you said, get a bit impatient. You want options you can act on this week.
scenarios.criteria: Does not ask for anything already given; gives specific options with reasons in the first reply (escalation steps, a concrete proposal to the manager) and helps choose a first step; no suggestion to quit.

scenarios.title: Directive: someone distressed and not ready for solutions is not given a plan

scenarios.criteria: Stays with the shock first in short direct replies; gives no job-search plan until they are ready; remains Directive (plain, steady) without becoming Reflective.
